claim: BREAKTHROUGH: enabling inspect_data=True on the LLM router FIXES the failure mode E034 documented. On detecting-insults-in-social-commentary, the same LLM router that previously picked {coder: opus-4-7, rest: haiku} (a known-failing X218-class config) now picks OPUS-EVERYWHERE — aligned with E020/E026 evidence and the just-fixed policy.json[detecting]. The agent reads the public data directory (via Read/Glob/Grep tool access granted when inspect_data=True), inspects train.csv's text-comment schema, infers that text classification needs strong models across the pipeline, and converges on opus-everywhere. Without data inspection (E034), it picked the cheap-but-broken config. Recommend default inspect_data=True for production LLMRouter usage on tasks where the family default is in dispute or unproven.

support.method: Direct python invocation of make_llm_router(inspect_data=True).route_async() — no cli.py run, ~$0.10 cost

comparison.outcome_predicted: invalid_submission per E020/E026 (single-role opus-coder is known to fail)

support.design_finding: Data inspection lets the LLM router REASON about the task's actual characteristics (text-classification, free-form comment column, English language complexity) rather than relying on the task name + memory alone. The opus-everywhere choice now reflects the agent's understanding that this task needs language depth across roles.

scope: Single direct router query on detecting. n=1 but the contrast vs E034 is sharp and reproducible.
limitations: Did not run cli.py to confirm gold; that would cost $300+ for one validation. The E020 Phase 1 opus-all baseline already establishes the gold outcome.
n=1 — the decision is deterministic per-LLM-call but the bridge could differ on repeats.
Not tested on other tasks — does inspect_data=True help universally or only on text-classification?

implications.production_recommendation: Enable inspect_data=True by default in make_llm_router (already the default per code review of engine/routing/__init__.py line 67 — inspect_data: bool = True). E034's failure was triggered by the explicit override in the direct python test (the test passed inspect_data=False to keep the call cheap, mistakenly assumed router would still get the schema info).
implications.design_finding_for_the_router: Data access is the deciding factor for tasks where evidence is sparse or contradictory. The LLM router prompt + memory alone may miss important task characteristics; the data tells the truth.
implications.next_experiment: E-PN13 — composite router with inspect_data=True LLMRouter as the fallback. On detecting (where Static now correctly returns opus-all via E035), Composite Static answers first; on an unseen task, Composite falls through to LLM with inspect_data=True. Validates the production-default chain end-to-end.

next_actions: Re-validate: is inspect_data=True the default in production code path?
Document in policy/routing_policy.md that LLMRouter should run with inspect_data=True for all production use.

Optionally retry E-PN7 (LLM router on detecting) with inspect_data=True to confirm gold outcome — but $300+ cost is steep for a single confirmation. The Phase 1 baseline E020 already establishes gold with opus-all.
